key_insight: Weak, low-frequency sinusoidal forcing can substantially reshape turbulence and increase inertial-particle clustering in a planar jet, even though the mean flow changes little.
engineering_relevance: Periodic modulation offers a potential control knob for particle distribution and mixing in jets, with implications for sprays, combustion, and particulate transport systems.
method: Hot-wire anemometry measured carrier-flow turbulence at two Reynolds numbers.
High-speed particle imaging and Voronoi tessellation quantified preferential concentration of dilute inertial droplets.
Forced and unforced jets were compared over the forcing cycle to relate turbulence scales, Stokes number, and clustering.
evidence_signal: Across two Reynolds numbers, forcing reduced the integral scale by up to 40% and increased preferential concentration, with phase-dependent clustering variations of 21–49% of the cycle mean.
watch_item: The study is specific to weak periodic forcing in a planar jet, so the observed clustering control may not transfer directly to other geometries, forcing amplitudes, or particle loading regimes.
paper_title: Preferential concentration in a periodically forced particle-laden turbulent planar jet
